title: Before the Burial
summary: After two days and two nights, people are about to take a man's body to a sepulchre made for burying their dead. The queen, having heard of Ammon's fame, sends for him.
locations: a sepulchre made for burying the dead

explicit_facts.text: After two days and two nights, people were about to take his body and lay it in a sepulchre made for burying their dead.
The queen had heard of Ammon's fame and sent, desiring that he come to her.

unspecified_visual_details: The man's identity and appearance.
The appearance of the sepulchre.

title: The queen speaks with Ammon
summary: Ammon went to the queen and sought to know what she wanted him to do. She told him what her husband's servants had said about him and asked him to see her husband. She said her husband had lain on his bed for two days and two nights, reported differing opinions about whether he was dead, and said he did not stink to her.
locations: An unspecified place where Ammon meets the queen

explicit_facts.text: Ammon went to the queen and sought to know what she wanted him to do.
The queen said her husband's servants had told her that Ammon was a prophet of a holy God and had power to do many mighty works in his name.
The queen asked Ammon to see her husband, who had been laid on his bed for two days and two nights.
The queen said some believed her husband was not dead, while others believed he was dead and should be placed in the sepulchre. She said he did not stink to her.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon and the queen are close enough to converse.
unspecified_visual_details: Their clothing, the furnishings, and the precise setting of their conversation.

spoken_dialogue.text: I would that ye should go in and see my husband,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The queen of Lamoni

narration.text: And it came to pass that Ammon did as he was commanded, and went in unto the queen, and desired to know what she would that he should do.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ammon's question is narrated, not supplied as direct speech. The servants' report and the differing opinions about the queen's husband are conveyed by the queen, not shown as separate events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give Ammon a verbatim spoken question.

title: Ammon and the queen

Ammon asks the queen whether she believes this. She says she has no witness except his word and the servants’ word, but believes him.
Ammon blesses the queen for her exceeding faith and compares it with faith among the Nephites.

title: The king rises
summary: At the appointed time, the king rises, reaches toward the queen, and speaks of seeing his Redeemer. He sinks again with joy, and the queen sinks down, overpowered by the Spirit.

explicit_facts.text: The king arose according to Ammon’s words, stretched out his hand to the queen, and blessed God and her.

The king said he had seen his Redeemer, who would be born of a woman and redeem believers. His heart swelled within him and he sank again with joy; the queen also sank down, overpowered by the Spirit.

unspecified_visual_details: The Redeemer’s appearance; he is mentioned but not described as visibly present.

title: Ammon and the servants fall
summary: Ammon kneels in prayer and thanksgiving, is overcome with joy, and sinks to the earth with two others. Seeing them fallen, the king’s servants cry unto God and call on his name until all have fallen except Abish.
characters: Two others among the three who sank to the earth, unidentified in the supplied verses

explicit_facts.text: Ammon saw the Spirit of the Lord poured out upon the Lamanites according to his prayers.
Ammon knelt and began to pray and give thanks to God; overcome with joy, he was among three who sank to the earth.
The king’s servants saw that they had fallen and began to cry unto God because the fear of the Lord had come upon them.
These servants had previously testified before the king concerning the great power of Ammon.
The servants called on the name of the Lord until all had fallen to the earth except Abish, a Lamanitish woman.
Abish had been converted unto the Lord for many years on account of a remarkable vision of her father.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities of the other two among the three who sank to the earth in verse 14.
The exact number and appearance of the servants.

title: The multitude gathers
summary: A multitude assembles at the king’s house and sees the king, queen, and servants lying prostrate, as well as Ammon. Some people murmur about the cause. Others rebuke them, and men who had scattered the king’s flocks also rebuke them.

explicit_facts.text: A multitude came to the king’s house and saw the king, queen, and servants lying prostrate as though dead.
The people also saw Ammon, who was a Nephite.
Some people attributed the evil they perceived to the king’s allowing the Nephite to remain in the land.
Others rebuked them and blamed the king for slaying servants whose flocks had been scattered at the waters of Sebus.
Men who had scattered the king’s flocks also rebuked them. They were angry with Ammon because he had slain some of their brethren while defending the flocks.

title: The multitude disputes Ammon’s identity
summary: People offer conflicting claims about Ammon, and their contention becomes exceedingly sharp. The woman servant who gathered the multitude comes, sees the contention, and is moved to tears.

explicit_facts.text: Many said Ammon was the Great Spirit; others said he was sent by the Great Spirit.
Others rebuked them, saying Ammon was a monster sent from the Nephites to torment them.
Some said Ammon was sent by the Great Spirit to afflict them because of their iniquities. They also attributed the Nephites’ deliverance and the destruction of many Lamanites to the Great Spirit.
The contention became exceedingly sharp. The woman servant who had gathered the multitude came, saw the contention, and was sorrowful even unto tears.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Members of the multitude dispute with one another.
